subject: SLO & benchmark sync — throughput / latency confirmation and prompt pack
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Li <jordan.li@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLO & benchmark sync — throughput / latency confirmation and prompt pack

Hi Jordan — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick written recap and concrete next steps so we have everything in one place.

Call recap (short):
- Goal: qualify Redwood for production inference on your catalog-retrieval flow and a streaming chat use case.
- Primary SLO constraints you flagged: latency for short completions (prompt ~150 tokens) and streaming tail behavior, plus a sustained concurrency target for peak traffic.
- Success criteria (your ask): p95 latency under 300ms for the catalog prompt baseline, ability to sustain ~250 concurrent inference streams with bounded tail latency, and end-to-end streaming event latency <500ms for first token.

What we need from you to start a reproducible bench run:
1) Prompt pack: canonical prompt+context pairs (100-200 examples), with tokenization expectations and expected output checks.
2) Traffic profile: concurrency targets, request arrival distribution (burstiness), and representative input sizes for both catalog and chat flows.
3) Any network egress constraints (VPC/cloud region) and privacy/retention musts.

What we'll deliver back:
- A measurement spec (definitions for p50/p95/p99, how we measure streaming first-token latency, throughput windows).
- An eval harness config (continuous-batching parameters, simulated concurrency generator, kv/prefix caching on/off).
- Draft SLO matrix with pass/fail thresholds tied to your acceptance criteria.

Attachments I uploaded to the shared Drive: initial benchmark template (harness_template_v2.yaml) and an SLO matrix skeleton (slo_matrix_acme.xlsx). Please add your prompt pack to the Drive folder or attach to a reply.

Next steps / dates:
- Jordan: drop prompt pack to the Drive or reply with attached prompt JSON by EOD Wed (2027-03-24).
- Us (Marissa + Soojin): produce measurement spec and a runnable harness by Fri (2027-03-26) so you can run it or we can run it on your behalf.
- Tune: follow-on call to review initial run — propose 2027-03-29.

If those timelines look OK, I'll record them in HubSpot and assign the harness work to Marissa.

Thanks —
Jonas

Subject: Re: SLO & benchmark sync — throughput / latency confirmation and prompt pack

Thanks Jonas — that matches my notes. Quick clarifications before we drop prompts: 

- The 250 concurrent streams is our expected peak for Black Friday-like events; average concurrency is ~40 during normal traffic. For qualification please run both steady-state (40) and spike (250) with realistic burst patterns (Poisson + 10s trapezoidal ramp).
- For the catalog flow: prompts are shorter (~80-160 tokens) with a small retrieval context (up to 512 tokens total). For chat/streaming: history length max 1k tokens; first-token latency is our blocker.
- We have a soft requirement that p99 for streaming-first-token be <800ms; p95 target for short completions is 300ms (hard requirement for the pilot).

I'll upload a labeled prompt pack (100 samples per flow) tonight and include expected matching criteria (BLEU + simple regex checks) — attaching initial filenames below.

Jordan
Jordan Li
Engineering Manager, Platform
Acme Retail
jordan.li@acme-retail.com

Attachments (will upload): acme_catalog_prompts_v1.json, acme_chat_prompts_v1.json
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Li <jordan.li@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLO & benchmark sync — throughput / latency confirmation and prompt pack

Jordan — appreciate the specificity, this is exactly what we need. A couple of concrete notes from the engineering side: 

- Measurement definitions: we'll run the catalog flow as synchronous requests (no streaming) and report tokenized p50/p95/p99 measured at the model output completion. For the streaming chat flow we'll capture first-byte (first token) latency and full-stream completion times separately. We'll include both client-to-model and model-to-client windows in the streaming first-token metric.
- Harness details: the harness_template_v2.yaml we shared contains toggles for prefix caching, KV cache warmup runs, batch size caps, and simulated network RTT. Please confirm whether you want cache-warmup included (recommended) or a cold-cache baseline run (helpful for worst-case).
- Reproducibility: please include a deterministic seed for any sampling in the prompt pack and note if any prompts include randomized elements. Also list the model variant you expect to test (e.g., rw-instruct-70b-qat/latest or a 8-bit quantized variant).

Action items from us:
- Marissa: produce a finished measurement-spec doc (definitions + scripts) by Thu 2027-03-25.
- Soojin: prepare the harness with the concurrency generator and a sample run profile; will post harness YAML and a short runbook to Drive.
- Rishi: evaluate whether we should run qualification in Redwood-hosted infra or in your VPC; cost/duration estimates forthcoming.

Jordan — once you upload the prompt pack I'll seed an initial run and share raw traces + aggregated metrics. If you prefer we can run the qualification in your environment to remove network variability.

- Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: SLO & benchmark sync — throughput / latency confirmation and prompt pack

Jordan / team — I've dropped a harness stub into the shared Drive (harness_template_v2.yaml) and included a sample concurrency profile (spike + steady windows). The harness includes:
- A concurrency generator that supports sustained and ramped-load patterns (JSON profile).
- First-token instrumentation hooks (client-side timestamps + model-side emission tag).
- Options for cold vs warm cache runs; default is warm with two warmup iterations per model shard.

Drive links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-example-drive-link (prompt pack folder)
File stubs: harness_template_v2.yaml (config), run_profile_spike.json, runbook_quickstart.md

Notes on running:
- If you're uploading the prompt pack, please include a small manifest.json with 'seed' and 'tokenization' fields. That makes runs deterministic across environments.
- For streaming runs, the harness will emit two CSVs per run: first_token_latency.csv and stream_completion_latency.csv. We'll provide a small parser to produce p50/p95/p99 and the 99.9 tail.

I'll also attach the harness config to this thread (see attachments). Happy to hop on a short run-through demo if you or your infra team want it.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Inference Performance Lead, Redwood Inference

- Jordan: confirm the deterministic seed and whether you want warm-cache baselines included by EOD today (2027-03-24).

I'll log the plan in HubSpot (deal RDW-ACME-2027-Q2-48) and schedule the follow-up calibration call for 2027-03-29 10:00 PT — calendar invite to follow.

If anything changes on your side (e.g., additional prompt sets, tweaks to pass/fail checks), reply-all and we'll iterate. Looking forward to a repeatable run and clear pass criteria.

Best —
Jonas
